subject: Re: [unmarked] ranef() warning message: In dbinom(ya[i, j, t], N, pa[i, j, t]) : non-integer x

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] ranef() warning message: In dbinom(ya[i, j, t], N, pa[i, j, t]) : non-integer x
parts:
hi Kaz,
 I recommend against using the N-mixture models for your situation. I'm guessing there is so much variation in N at that level of abundance that the model can't possibly produce meaningful predictions (not to mention the computational problem you encountered).
 The warning message seems to be due to the scaling. dbinom() has to take integer arguments.
regards
andy



On Tue, May 14, 2013 at 8:41 PM, Kaz <kazl...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I'm trying to estimate yearly abundance of birds at 33 sites over 20 years, with 4 counts per year. Counts range from 0 to 6600 individuals, with lots of NAs. I've therefore had to use scale() to prevent pcountOpen() from crashing R with such a large K.

However, when I then try to use ranef(), I therefore get the following  warning messages (which is not surprising as I have scaled bird counts so they are no longer an integer):


> re <- ranef(m1)
There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
> warnings()
Warning messages:
1: In dbinom(ya[i, j, t], N, pa[i, j, t]) : non-integer x = -0.276340
2: In dbinom(ya[i, j, t], N, pa[i, j, t]) : non-integer x = -0.276340
etc...
> re
Error in out[, , t] <- cbind(means[, t], modes[, t], CI[, , t]) : 
  incorrect number of subscripts

Is there a way to work around this?

Thanks,
Kaz

Here's my code if it's any help:

> library(unmarked)
> barwit.umf <- unmarkedFramePCO(y=scale(counts),   
+                                siteCovs=(data.frame(data$roost.type,data$Distance.from.RM)),
+                                obsCovs=list(tide=tide,date=date,wind=wind,SOI=SOI),
+                                yearlySiteCovs=list(WaterQuality=WQ,Temp=T,Rainfall=Prcp),
+                                numPrimary=20)
 

> siteCovs(barwit.umf) <- scale(siteCovs(barwit.umf))
> siteCovs(barwit.umf) <- scale(siteCovs(barwit.umf))
> obsCovs(barwit.umf) <- scale(obsCovs(barwit.umf))
> yearlySiteCovs(barwit.umf)<-scale(yearlySiteCovs(barwit.umf))

#Very simple model with tide height as a covariate for detection probability
> (m1 <-  pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1, ~tide, barwit.umf, K=30))

> f<-backTransform(linearComb(m1, matrix(c(1, 2.2),1,2), type="det"))

messages.author: d31b935caf8728c5
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] ranef() warning message: In dbinom(ya[i, j, t], N, pa[i, j, t]) : non-integer x
parts:
Thanks Andy,

To be more precise the data I have is for shorebirds during the non breeding season, with counts taken while the birds are roosting. There are therefore either 0 or hundreds of birds visible during a count. The total population across the sites does not vary much, though it does appear to be declining; 20 years ago you would get counts of 6000 birds, now, no larger than 2000.

Would it be worthwhile aggregating some of the sites together (where we know the birds are either at one roost or the other) to reduce some of the variation in the data? The problem of the high K would remain though because the counts are still big. Is there not a good way to scale/transform the data so that ranef() can deal with it?

Would it be worthwhile even doing it in JAGS?

Thanks for the help,
Kaz

parts:
hi Kaz,
 I don't think this class of models is really very appropriate for the data you have, so my recommendation is to not use them. Alternatively, I suggest a standard type of GLMM which somehow you can fit in R using existing packages for doing those things.
regards,
andy
